name: OMS Ship-To Address And Phone Lookup Logic
purpose: Reusable rules for another project to look up a sales order's Ship To Address and the corresponding phone number by S/O number.

production_safety_notice.environment: This describes the real Jia Hua OMS production schema behavior.
production_safety_notice.warning: Use this file for SELECT/read logic. Do not use it to guess-write unknown fields. Do not alter/drop/truncate production tables.

orders.role: Sales order header. This is the first source for the actual ship-to address saved on an order.

important_fields.STORE_NUM: Selected chain-store number, when a chain store was selected.
important_fields.SP_ADR_22: Saved ship-to address line 2; often blank.
important_fields.CUS_SHIP_CHG: Despite the name, legacy OMS uses this decimal field to store the numeric phone printed for the ship-to/order after reopening an order.
important_fields.CUS_SHIP_TEL2: Web app compatibility phone field. Legacy OMS historical orders are usually NULL here.

customer.role: Customer master. Used for fallback bill-to/default ship-to information and phone.

important_fields.PHONE_2: Customer fax/secondary phone depending on OMS usage.
important_fields.SHP_CUS_NM: Default shipping name, if separate shipping exists.

important_fields.PHONE: Store phone. Can be blank for some stores.

S.expected_related_field: orders.STORE_NUM should normally point to chn_str.STR_NUM.
S.write_rule_used_by_web_app: Use S only when STORE_NUM is present.

N.meaning: Customer has separate SHP_* default shipping fields and no chain store was selected.
N.example: Customer 7186639333 has SHP_ADDRESS=TEST2. Legacy OMS order 11469 uses SP_SM_ADR=N.

Y.meaning: Normal billing/default ship-to order, usually no separate customer SHP_* fields and no selected store.
Y.common_case: Most single-address customers without chain stores use Y.

sp_sm_adr_meaning.important_bug_note: Do not set SP_SM_ADR=S just because the order has non-empty SP_ADR/SP_ADR_2. That can make legacy OMS reopen/print use the wrong path and show phone as 0000000000.

address_lookup_algorithm_by_so_number: 1. SELECT the order row from dbo.orders by ORD_NUM.
2. LEFT JOIN dbo.customer on customer.CUS_ID = orders.CUS_ID.
3. If orders.STORE_NUM is non-empty, LEFT JOIN dbo.chn_str on CUS_ID and STR_NUM.
4. For the actual saved order address, prefer orders.SP_ADR, SP_ADR_2, SP_ADR_22, SP_ADR_CT, SP_ADR_ST, SP_ADR_ZP, and SP_ADR_3.
5. If the order SP_ADR fields are missing and STORE_NUM exists, fall back to the matching chn_str store row.
6. If no store row applies and customer SHP_* fields exist, fall back to customer.SHP_* fields.
7. Otherwise fall back to customer billing fields CUS_NM, ADDRESS, ADDRESS2, CITY, STATE, ZIP.

for_matching_legacy_oms_print: 1. Prefer orders.CUS_SHIP_CHG when it is non-null and not zero. Convert decimal digits to a phone string.
2. If CUS_SHIP_CHG is zero/blank and orders.CUS_SHIP_TEL2 is non-empty, use CUS_SHIP_TEL2. This catches web-created orders before/around the compatibility fix.
3. If STORE_NUM is present and the matching chn_str.PHONE is non-empty, use chn_str.PHONE.
4. If customer.SHP_PHONE is non-empty, use customer.SHP_PHONE.
6. If all sources are blank, report blank/unknown instead of inventing 0000000000.
phone_lookup_algorithm_by_so_number.why_cus_ship_chg_first: Legacy OMS orders usually leave CUS_SHIP_TEL2 NULL. The phone that legacy OMS prints after reopening an order is represented by the numeric digits in orders.CUS_SHIP_CHG.
phone_lookup_algorithm_by_so_number.formatting_rule: Strip non-digits. If 10 digits, display as (AAA) BBB-CCCC when needed. Keep raw digits for database comparisons.

recommended_select_shape.description: SQL Server query shape for one S/O. Keep this read-only.
sql: c.CUS_NM, c.ADDRESS, c.ADDRESS2, c.CITY, c.STATE, c.ZIP,
c.SHP_CUS_NM, c.SHP_ADDRESS, c.SHP_ADDRESS2, c.SHP_CITY, c.SHP_STATE, c.SHP_ZIP, c.SHP_PHONE,
s.STR_NUM, s.CUS_NM AS storeName, s.ADDRESS AS storeAddress, s.ADDRESS2 AS storeAddress2,
s.CITY AS storeCity, s.STATE AS storeState, s.ZIP AS storeZip, s.PHONE AS storePhone
LEFT JOIN dbo.customer AS c ON c.CUS_ID = o.CUS_ID

phone_conversion_sql_snippet.description: Convert orders.CUS_SHIP_CHG decimal digits into a varchar phone candidate.

10617.observed_problem: Web print showed phone, but reopening/printing in legacy OMS showed 0000000000.
10617.lesson: SP_SM_ADR=S was wrong for this non-store customer, and CUS_SHIP_CHG was missing.

11469.source: Legacy OMS-created order for same customer as 10617
11469.lesson: For customer with default SHP_* shipping fields and no selected store, legacy OMS uses SP_SM_ADR=N and stores printed phone digits in CUS_SHIP_CHG.

customer_3475251935.description: Multi-store customer DML DOLLAR CENTRAL INC.
lessons: Orders selecting a store normally use SP_SM_ADR=S and STORE_NUM matching chn_str.STR_NUM.
Store phone may be blank. In historical OMS orders, CUS_SHIP_CHG can be 0 when the selected store has no phone.
For extracting a corresponding phone, use CUS_SHIP_CHG first when nonzero, then store/customer fallback depending on the desired display behavior.

implementation_notes: For a saved order, the orders.SP_ADR* fields are the most faithful address source because they represent what was saved at order time.
For matching legacy OMS print behavior, do not ignore CUS_SHIP_CHG even though its name sounds like a charge amount.
For web/display robustness, CUS_SHIP_TEL2 can be used as fallback because some web-created orders may have that field populated while CUS_SHIP_CHG is zero.
If your project only reads data, do not update SP_SM_ADR, CUS_SHIP_CHG, or CUS_SHIP_TEL2.
If another project writes orders, use the SP_SM_ADR write rule above and write CUS_SHIP_CHG with the chosen phone digits inside the same transaction as the order header.
